title: Can You Really Do Two Things at Once?
subtitle: 你真的能一心多用嗎？任務切換的代價
source: 原創議題文章；依 Rubinstein, Meyer & Evans（2001）、Strayer & Johnston（2001）、Ophir, Nass & Wagner（PNAS, 2009）、Uncapher & Wagner（PNAS, 2018）摘要核對，2026-10-22

sources.title: Rubinstein, J. S., Meyer, D. E. & Evans, J. E. (2001). Executive control of cognitive processes in task switching. JEP: Human Perception and Performance.
Strayer, D. L. & Johnston, W. A. (2001). Driven to distraction: dual-task studies of simulated driving and conversing on a cellular telephone. Psychological Science.
Ophir, E., Nass, C. & Wagner, A. D. (2009). Cognitive control in media multitaskers. PNAS 106(37).
Uncapher, M. R. & Wagner, A. D. (2018). Minds and brains of media multitaskers: current findings and future directions. PNAS 115(40).

beginner.title: Switching, Not Doing Both
paras: You are doing your homework. Your phone buzzes, so you check a message. Then you go back to your homework. Then you watch a short video. Many students do this every day and call it “multitasking”. They believe they are doing two things at once. But are they?
你正在寫作業。手機震動了，你看了一下訊息，然後回到作業上，接著又看了一支短影片。很多學生每天都這樣做，還稱之為「一心多用」。他們相信自己同時在做兩件事。但真的是這樣嗎？

Scientists say that, for most tasks that need thinking, our brains do not really do two things at the same time. Instead, they switch quickly from one task to the other. Each switch takes a little time, and the time is longer when the tasks are difficult. Switching to a new, unfamiliar task takes even longer.
科學家說，對大多數需要思考的任務來說，大腦其實並不是同時做兩件事，而是在兩件事之間快速切換。每次切換都要花一點時間；任務越難，花的時間越長。切換到一個陌生的新任務，花的時間更長。

Talking on the phone while driving is a dangerous example. In one study, people used a driving simulator. When they talked on a phone, they missed twice as many traffic signals. It did not matter if they held the phone or used a hands-free one. But listening to the radio or an audiobook did not cause this problem. The trouble came from having a real conversation.
邊開車邊講電話是一個危險的例子。在一項研究中，人們使用駕駛模擬器。當他們講電話時，漏看交通號誌的次數變成兩倍。不管是手持電話還是使用免持裝置，結果都一樣。但聽廣播或有聲書並不會造成這個問題。麻煩來自真正的對話。

In 2009, researchers at Stanford compared people who often use many kinds of media at once with people who rarely do. Surprisingly, the heavy multitaskers were worse at ignoring things that did not matter. They were even worse at switching between tasks.
2009 年，史丹佛的研究人員比較了常常同時使用多種媒體的人和很少這樣做的人。出人意料的是，常一心多用的人比較不會忽略不重要的東西，連在任務之間切換的能力也比較差。

Scientists are still studying whether multitasking causes these problems, or whether easily distracted people simply multitask more. But the advice is simple: when you study, put your phone away and focus on one thing at a time.
科學家仍在研究，是一心多用造成這些問題，還是容易分心的人本來就比較常一心多用。但建議很簡單：讀書時，把手機收起來，一次只專心做一件事。

intermediate.title: Can You Really Do Two Things at Once?
paras: Homework on the laptop, messages on the phone, a video playing in another tab: for many students, this is simply what studying looks like. People often describe it as multitasking and assume they are doing several things at once. Psychological research suggests that, for tasks that require attention and thought, what we actually do is something different.
筆電上寫作業、手機上回訊息、另一個分頁播著影片：對許多學生來說，這就是讀書的樣子。人們常把這稱為一心多用，並以為自己同時在做好幾件事。心理學研究顯示，對於需要注意力和思考的任務，我們實際上做的是另一回事。

Instead of doing tasks simultaneously, the brain usually switches between them, and each switch has a cost. In a 2001 series of experiments, participants alternated between tasks such as classifying shapes or solving arithmetic problems. Switching took extra time, and these “switching costs” increased when the rules were more complex. Clear cues about which task to do next reduced the cost, but did not remove it. Switching from a familiar task to an unfamiliar one took longer than switching in the opposite direction.
大腦通常不是同時做多件事，而是在它們之間切換，而每次切換都有代價。在 2001 年的一系列實驗中，參與者在分類圖形或解算術題等任務之間交替。切換需要額外的時間，而且規則越複雜，這種「切換成本」就越高。清楚提示下一個要做的任務，能降低成本，卻無法消除它。從熟悉的任務切換到陌生的任務，比反方向切換花的時間更長。

The consequences can be serious. In a driving-simulator study published in 2001, conversations on a mobile phone doubled the number of simulated traffic signals that drivers failed to notice, and slowed their reactions to the signals they did see. Importantly, hands-free phones were no safer. Listening to the radio or an audiobook did not cause the same problem; the trouble came from being engaged in a conversation. Simply repeating words heard on the phone did not disrupt driving, but a task that required thinking of new words did — and the effect grew when the driving was harder.
後果可能很嚴重。在 2001 年發表的一項駕駛模擬研究中，用手機通話讓駕駛人漏看的模擬交通號誌數量變成兩倍，對看到的號誌反應也變慢了。重要的是，免持電話並沒有比較安全。聽廣播或有聲書不會造成同樣的問題；麻煩來自投入一場對話。只是複述電話裡聽到的字詞，並不會干擾駕駛；但需要想出新字詞的任務就會——而且駕駛難度越高，影響越大。

What about people who multitask all the time — do they get better at it? A 2009 Stanford study compared heavy and light media multitaskers. The heavy multitaskers were more easily distracted by irrelevant information around them and in their memory. Surprisingly, they also performed worse on a test of switching between tasks — the very skill they practised most.
那些一天到晚一心多用的人呢——他們會因此變得更厲害嗎？2009 年一項史丹佛的研究比較了重度與輕度的媒體多工者。重度多工者更容易被周遭和記憶中不相關的資訊分心。令人意外的是，他們在任務切換的測驗上表現也更差——而那正是他們最常練習的技能。

A 2018 review of later research urged caution: many studies have found no differences, and it is not yet clear whether multitasking causes weaker attention or whether people with weaker attention multitask more. Still, the balance of evidence points in one direction. If you want to learn something well, protecting your attention may matter more than trying to do everything at once.
2018 年一篇整理後續研究的回顧則提醒要謹慎：許多研究並沒有發現差異，而且目前還不清楚，是一心多用造成注意力變弱，還是注意力較弱的人本來就比較常一心多用。儘管如此，整體證據仍指向同一個方向：如果你想把東西學好，保護你的注意力，可能比試圖同時做完所有事更重要。

advanced.title: The Hidden Costs of Task Switching
paras: Contemporary students rarely study without interruption. Assignments compete with messages, notifications and videos, and many young people describe themselves as skilled multitaskers. The concept, however, rests on an assumption that psychological research has repeatedly challenged: that the mind can perform several demanding tasks in parallel. For tasks that require attention and executive control, the evidence suggests that what feels like simultaneous activity is usually rapid alternation, and that alternation is never free.
當代學生很少能不受打擾地讀書。作業與訊息、通知和影片互相競爭，許多年輕人也自認擅長一心多用。然而，這個概念建立在一個心理學研究一再挑戰的假設上：心智能平行執行好幾項高要求的任務。對於需要注意力與執行控制的任務，證據顯示，那種感覺像是同時進行的活動，通常是快速的交替，而交替從來都不是免費的。

Laboratory studies have measured these costs directly. In a 2001 set of four experiments, Rubinstein, Meyer and Evans asked participants either to alternate between tasks — classifying geometric objects by different rules, or solving arithmetic problems using different operations — or to repeat the same task. Alternation produced switching-time costs that grew with rule complexity and shrank when visual cues indicated the next task. The researchers proposed a model in which executive control involves distinct stages of shifting goals and activating new rules, each of which consumes time.
實驗室研究直接測量了這些成本。在 2001 年的四項實驗中，魯賓斯坦、邁爾與埃文斯讓參與者在任務之間交替——依不同規則分類幾何物體，或用不同運算解算術題——或重複同一項任務。交替產生了切換時間成本，規則越複雜成本越高，而有視覺提示指出下一項任務時成本則會降低。研究者提出一個模型：執行控制包含「轉換目標」與「啟動新規則」兩個不同階段，每一個階段都會耗費時間。

The real-world implications are starkest on the road. In dual-task studies of simulated driving, Strayer and Johnston found that unconstrained mobile-phone conversations, whether handheld or hands-free, doubled the rate at which drivers failed to detect simulated traffic signals and slowed reactions to signals they did detect. Listening to the radio or to a book on tape caused no such disruption. The authors concluded that the danger lies not in holding the phone but in diverting attention to an engaging cognitive context other than driving. Simply repeating words heard over a handheld phone did not impair driving, whereas a task requiring participants to generate words did, and the deficit grew as driving became more difficult.

真實世界的影響在道路上最為明顯。在模擬駕駛的雙重任務研究中，斯特雷耶和約翰斯頓發現，不受限制的手機通話——無論手持或免持——都讓駕駛人漏看模擬交通號誌的比例加倍，對看到的號誌反應也變慢。聽廣播或錄音書則沒有造成這種干擾。作者的結論是：危險不在於拿著手機，而在於把注意力轉移到駕駛以外、另一個引人投入的認知情境中。只是複述手持電話中聽到的字詞，並不會影響駕駛；但要求參與者自己想出字詞的任務則會，而且駕駛越困難，表現下降得越多。

A natural assumption is that practice improves multitasking. In 2009, however, Ophir, Nass and Wagner at Stanford developed an index to identify heavy and light media multitaskers and compared them on standard measures of cognitive control. Heavy multitaskers were more susceptible to interference from irrelevant stimuli and from irrelevant representations in memory. Paradoxically, they also performed worse on a test of task-switching ability, apparently because they were less able to filter out the task they were no longer supposed to be doing.
一個自然的假設是：練習會讓一心多用變得更厲害。然而在 2009 年，史丹佛的奧菲爾、納斯與華格納設計了一套指標來區分重度與輕度媒體多工者，並用標準的認知控制測量加以比較。重度多工者更容易受到不相關刺激以及記憶中不相關表徵的干擾。弔詭的是，他們在任務切換能力的測驗上表現也更差，似乎是因為他們比較無法過濾掉已經不該再做的那項任務。

Subsequent research has complicated, though not overturned, this picture. A 2018 review by Uncapher and Wagner noted that the literature remains sparse and mixed, that many studies find no differences between groups, and that the direction of causality is unknown: multitasking might weaken attention, or people with weaker sustained attention might simply multitask more. Even so, where differences appear, heavier multitaskers tend to perform worse on tasks requiring sustained, goal-directed attention. For learners, the practical conclusion is modest but robust: deep understanding depends on attention, and attention is easier to protect than to recover once it has been divided.

後續研究讓這幅圖像變得更複雜，但並沒有推翻它。烏恩卡弗與華格納在 2018 年的回顧中指出，相關文獻仍然稀少且結果不一，許多研究並未發現兩組之間有差異，而且因果方向未明：可能是一心多用削弱了注意力，也可能只是持續注意力較弱的人比較常一心多用。即便如此，在出現差異的研究中，重度多工者在需要持續、目標導向注意力的任務上，往往表現較差。對學習者而言，實際的結論溫和卻穩固：深度理解有賴於注意力，而注意力一旦被分散，要找回來遠比事先保護它困難。

quote.text: Heavy media multitaskers performed worse on a test of task-switching ability, likely due to reduced ability to filter out interference from the irrelevant task set.
quote.author: Ophir, Nass & Wagner

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to send messages faster while studying.
Why doing two thinking tasks at once rarely works.
Why the radio is dangerous for drivers.
How Stanford students use social media.
beginner.evidence: our brains do not really do two things at the same time
beginner.why: 全文：大腦其實是在任務間切換，切換有代價。
traps: 正反顛倒：作者建議讀書時把手機收起來。
正反顛倒：聽廣播沒有造成問題。
以偏概全：史丹佛研究只是其中一項。

beginner.q: What does “this problem” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Switching to a new task.
Holding a phone in one hand.
Listening to an audiobook.
Missing traffic signals while driving.
beginner.evidence: they missed twice as many traffic signals
beginner.why: 前文：講電話時漏看的交通號誌多了一倍。
traps: 時序錯置：切換任務是第二段的內容。
正反顛倒：用不用手持沒差別。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：聽有聲書不會造成問題。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Hands-free phones were no safer than handheld ones.
Listening to the radio doubled missed signals.
Heavy multitaskers were better at switching tasks.
Switching to a new task takes less time.
beginner.evidence: It did not matter if they held the phone or used a hands-free one.
traps: 張冠李戴：聽廣播沒有影響。
正反顛倒：他們更不會切換。
正反顛倒：切換到陌生任務更久。

beginner.q: What does the writer advise students to do?
options: Watch short videos to rest the brain.
Check messages between every homework question.
Put the phone away and focus on one thing.
Study while talking on the phone.
beginner.evidence: put your phone away and focus on one thing at a time
traps: 捏造：文中沒有這種建議。
正反顛倒：這正是開頭描述的分心情況。
正反顛倒：對話最會分散注意。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Hands-free phones make driving completely safe.
Heavy multitaskers become better at everything over time.
Switching between tasks has costs, so focusing on one helps learning.
Clear cues remove all costs of switching tasks.
intermediate.evidence: protecting your attention may matter more than trying to do everything at once
traps: 正反顛倒：免持一樣危險。
正反顛倒：他們反而更容易分心。
正反顛倒：提示只能減少，不能消除。

intermediate.q: What does “simultaneously” in the second paragraph mean?
options: At the same time.
One after another.
Very slowly.
With great effort.
intermediate.evidence: Instead of doing tasks simultaneously, the brain usually switches between them
intermediate.why: 和 switches between them 對照：同時進行。
traps: 正反顛倒：那是 switch（輪流切換）。
字面誤讀：simultaneously 講的是「時間」，不是速度。
字面誤讀：這個字不是在說費力程度。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Listening to an audiobook doubled missed signals.
Thinking of new words made driving easier.
Clear cues completely removed switching costs.
Repeating words heard on the phone did not disrupt driving.
intermediate.evidence: Simply repeating words heard on the phone did not disrupt driving
traps: 張冠李戴：是講電話，不是聽有聲書。
正反顛倒：想新詞會干擾駕駛。
正反顛倒：只能減少成本。

intermediate.q: What does the 2018 review suggest about the research?
options: Multitasking has been proved to improve attention.
It is unclear whether multitasking causes weaker attention.
No study has ever found any difference.
Only drivers are affected by multitasking.
intermediate.evidence: it is not yet clear whether multitasking causes weaker attention or whether people with weaker attention multitask more
traps: 正反顛倒：沒有證據顯示會變好。
以偏概全：原文說 many studies，不是全部。
以偏概全：駕駛只是其中一例。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that practice makes people better multitaskers.
To prove that phones should be banned in cars.
To describe how geometric shapes are classified.
To show that multitasking usually means costly switching.
advanced.evidence: what feels like simultaneous activity is usually rapid alternation, and that alternation is never free
traps: 正反顛倒：常多工的人反而表現較差。
過度推論：作者沒有主張禁用。
以偏概全：那是實驗中的任務。

advanced.q: What does “executive control” in the second paragraph most likely refer to?
options: The power of company managers.
The mind’s ability to manage goals and rules.
The speed of reading simple words.
The habit of checking messages often.
advanced.evidence: executive control involves distinct stages of shifting goals and activating new rules
advanced.why: 同一句說明：轉換目標、啟動新規則。
traps: 字面誤讀：executive 不是公司主管。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：實驗任務是分類與算術，不是閱讀。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：那是分心的行為，不是控制能力。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Listening to the radio impaired drivers.
Visual cues made switching costs larger.
Heavy multitaskers did worse on a task-switching test.
Uncapher and Wagner found clear causes.
advanced.evidence: they also performed worse on a test of task-switching ability
traps: 正反顛倒：聽廣播沒有影響。
正反顛倒：提示讓成本變小。
正反顛倒：因果方向仍不明。

advanced.q: Why did heavy multitaskers do worse at switching tasks, according to the passage?
options: They found it harder to filter out the old task.
They practised task switching less than others did.
They were tested while driving real cars on roads.
They were given harder problems than the light group.
advanced.evidence: apparently because they were less able to filter out the task they were no longer supposed to be doing
traps: 正反顛倒：他們是最常練習的人。
張冠李戴：駕駛研究是模擬器。
捏造：兩組做的是相同測驗。

reflections: For one evening, record how many times you switch tasks while studying. Were you surprised by the number?
The 2018 review says we do not know the direction of cause and effect. Design a simple experiment that could help find out.

Listening to the radio or to a book on tape caused no such problem. It was not holding the phone that mattered, then, but being drawn into a conversation. Simply repeating words heard on the phone did not harm driving, whereas a task requiring drivers to think of new words did.
真實世界的影響在道路上最為明顯。在駕駛模擬研究中，史特雷爾和強斯頓發現，講電話——不論手持或免持——都讓駕駛漏看交通號誌的比率加倍，對看到的號誌反應也變慢。聽收音機或有聲書則不會造成這種問題。所以，重點不在手上拿著電話，而在被捲入一段對話。單純複述電話裡聽到的字不會影響駕駛，但要駕駛自己想出新詞的任務就會。

A natural assumption is that practice makes people better at multitasking. In 2009, however, Ophir, Nass and Wagner at Stanford compared heavy and light media multitaskers (people who often or rarely use several media at once). Heavy multitaskers were more easily distracted by irrelevant information around them and in their memory. Surprisingly, they also did worse on a test of switching between tasks, the very skill they practised most, apparently because they found it harder to filter out the task they had just left.
人們很自然地以為，多練習就會更擅長一心多用。然而 2009 年，史丹佛的歐菲爾、納斯和華格納比較了重度和輕度的媒體多工者（經常或很少同時使用多種媒體的人）。重度多工者比較容易被周遭和記憶中不相關的資訊干擾。令人意外的是，他們在任務切換測驗上的表現也比較差——這正是他們練習最多的技能——原因似乎是他們比較難濾掉剛剛離開的那項工作。

Later research has complicated, though not overturned, this picture. A 2018 review by Uncapher and Wagner noted that the evidence is limited and mixed, that many studies find no differences, and that the direction of cause is unknown: multitasking might weaken attention, or people with weaker attention might simply multitask more. Even so, the practical conclusion is clear. Deep understanding depends on attention, which is easier to protect than to win back once it has been divided.
後來的研究讓這幅圖像變得複雜，但沒有推翻它。2018 年，安卡佛和華格納的回顧指出，證據有限且分歧，許多研究沒有發現差異，而且因果方向不明：可能是多工削弱了注意力，也可能是注意力較弱的人本來就比較常多工。即便如此，實際的結論很清楚：深入的理解有賴於注意力，而注意力一旦被分散，保護它比事後找回來容易得多。
